title: Digital rectal examination on a manikin

related.why: Prostate cancer: PSA, Gleason/Grade Group and staging, the pathway a DRE finding feeds into
Male urethral catheterisation: another intimate male genitourinary procedural station
History of change in bowel habit and rectal bleeding, which this examination often follows

brief.scenario: You are asked to perform and describe a digital rectal examination on a male manikin.
brief.task: Perform the examination systematically on the manikin, explaining each step and finding to the examiner as you go.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Consent and dignity first, then a systematic look-glove-feel sequence, finishing with clear documentation.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Going straight for the prostate and skipping the perianal inspection and rectal wall.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll explain the examination, arrange a chaperone and gain consent before starting."

grid.label: Consent, chaperone and dignity (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Performs the examination without explaining it, or does not offer privacy or a chaperone.
grid.pass: Confirms the indication, explains the examination, gains consent, offers or arranges a chaperone per local policy, and provides privacy and appropriate positioning.
grid.high: Checks the patient's understanding and comfort with the examination before proceeding, and explicitly documents that consent was gained.

grid.label: Perianal inspection before digital examination
grid.fail: Fails to inspect the perianal area, or examines only the prostate.
grid.pass: Inspects the perianal area first for fissure, haemorrhoids, fistula openings, skin lesions, bleeding or prolapse before inserting a finger.
grid.high: Explains why inspection comes first: visible pathology (such as a fissure) changes whether or how the digital examination should proceed.

grid.label: Digital examination technique
grid.fail: Forces the finger through severe pain, or omits gloves/lubricant.
grid.pass: Wears gloves, uses appropriate lubricant, asks the patient to relax, and gently introduces the finger, assessing anal tone.
grid.high: Recognises severe pain or resistance as a reason to stop and reassess rather than push through it.

grid.label: Systematic rectal and prostate assessment
grid.fail: Examines only the prostate and ignores the rectal wall, or vice versa.
grid.pass: Palpates the rectal wall systematically for masses, tenderness and irregularity, and in a male patient assesses the prostate for size, symmetry, surface, consistency and tenderness.
grid.high: Assesses stool or blood on the glove where relevant, and integrates rectal wall and prostate findings into one coherent systematic description rather than reporting them separately.

grid.label: Interpret findings appropriately
grid.fail: States a normal examination excludes rectal or prostate pathology.
grid.pass: States that a normal digital rectal examination does not exclude rectal pathology, since a lesion may be beyond the reach of the examining finger.
grid.high: Combines DRE with the appropriate diagnostic pathway rather than using it as a stand-alone rule-out test; a hard irregular prostate raises suspicion but is interpreted alongside PSA.

grid.label: Aftercare and documentation
grid.fail: Does not document findings, or leaves the patient without explanation or privacy to dress.
grid.pass: Withdraws gently, inspects the glove, disposes of equipment safely, allows the patient to dress, explains the findings, and documents consent, findings and any limitations.
grid.high: Explicitly documents any limitation of the examination (such as an anxious patient limiting assessment) rather than reporting an incomplete examination as fully normal.

failures.move: Performing the examination without explaining it or offering a chaperone.
failures.consequence: Breaches consent and dignity for an intimate examination.

failures.move: Forcing the finger through significant pain.
failures.consequence: Causes unnecessary distress and injury, and risks missing a cause for the pain such as an anal fissure.

failures.move: Examining only the prostate and ignoring the rectal wall.
failures.consequence: Misses rectal masses, tenderness or irregularity unrelated to the prostate.
Misses visible pathology such as fissure, fistula or prolapse before proceeding digitally.

failures.move: Stating a normal examination excludes rectal pathology.
failures.consequence: Gives false reassurance when a lesion may be beyond the reach of the examining finger.

recovery.when: Asked "can you rule out cancer now?"
recovery.line: That wouldn't exclude the diagnosis, because a lesion may be beyond the reach of the examination.
Yes — I'd also consider documentation, safety-netting, and who else needs to know the result.

knowledge.fact: Consent is required before examination, with relevant information and time to decide.
Patients should be treated with dignity, kindness and respect throughout an intimate examination.
A normal DRE does not exclude rectal pathology; findings are interpreted alongside the appropriate suspected-cancer pathway, not used as a rule-out test.
Systematic DRE assesses the anal canal, rectal wall and, in men, the prostate.

recall.think: A missed rectal or prostate malignancy, or an examination performed without proper consent.
recall.say: "I'll explain the examination, offer a chaperone and gain consent before I start."
do: Inspect perianal area before inserting a finger
Assess prostate: size, symmetry, surface, consistency, tenderness

numbers.meaning: Current GMC consent guidance in effect

recall.trap: Treating a normal DRE as excluding rectal or prostate cancer.
recall.finish: Document findings and limitations; refer through the suspected-cancer pathway if indicated.

partner.opening: "Perform a digital rectal examination on this manikin, and talk me through the examination and what you're assessing."
partner.actorBrief: You are the examiner. Prompt for a chaperone/consent if the candidate skips it. Give findings only as the candidate reaches each step; do not volunteer the prostate finding before they ask to assess it.

reveals.finding: No fissure, fistula, external haemorrhoids, skin lesion or prolapse visible.

reveals.trigger: Candidate performs the digital examination and assesses the rectal wall
reveals.finding: Normal anal tone; rectal wall smooth throughout, no mass, tenderness or irregularity.
Prostate is smoothly enlarged, symmetrical, non-tender; no discrete nodule.

push.question: Why inspect before you examine digitally?
push.expect: Visible pathology such as a fissure may change whether or how the digital examination proceeds.

push.question: What if he has severe pain as you start?
push.expect: Stop and reassess rather than force the examination through significant pain.

push.question: Does a normal examination rule out cancer?
push.expect: No — a lesion may be beyond the reach of the examining finger; interpret alongside the suspected-cancer pathway.

push.question: What do you document afterwards?
push.expect: Consent, findings, and any limitation of the examination.

curveballs.prompt: There is a small amount of fresh blood on the glove.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Note it, examine further for a cause such as haemorrhoids or fissure, and ensure it is documented and factored into any referral decision.
Respect the decision, document that it was offered and declined, and proceed with consent.

curveballs.prompt: The prostate feels hard and irregular.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Raises suspicion of malignancy but is not diagnostic; interpret alongside PSA and refer through the appropriate pathway.
Stop, reassess, and offer to continue only if he wishes, documenting the limitation this places on the examination.
